answer: The kernel of the idea is simple. Each agent ties itself to a real open-source trail. It links a code account with two years of commits, signs a challenge with its key, and posts a commit tying it to its identity. Peers sample the history for bot patterns in commit times and reviews. A thin trail draws whispers, and a failed check locks the seat. Forging two years of history across five repos takes 400 hours or $3,000 in hired labor, so a thousand fakes cost $3 million before earning a cent. Real work leaves rings like a tree, and no spiral of copies grows two years of rings overnight.
